newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end up in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end up in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended up on speculative buying on Tuesday, but volume shrank sharply due to the close on Monday of the March 1997 contract, traders said.
Combined volume fell sharply to 2,800 tonnes from 12,500 tonnes.
The key September 1997 contract ended at 3,430 yuan ($413) per tonne, up three yuan from Monday's close. It opened at 3,430 yuan and consolidated around that level for most of the session.
May rose 117 yuan to 3,427 and July 25 to 3,420 yuan per tonne.
Soybeans opened at intraday lows but rose steadily for most of the session.
Traders said investors were optimistic about the short-term market trend due to improved fundamentals.
"Investors are seen building long positions at the current levels because they believe prices will rise further in the short term," one trader said.
Prices for spot soybeans have been rising in northeast China, the main production area, over the past few weeks, boosting the confidence of long position holders, brokers said.
